lines.text: What if the secret to glowing, glass skin... is rubbing snail slime on your face? It sounds strange, but this K-beauty ingredient has a real following.
If you've scrolled skincare TikTok, you've seen this gooey essence. Let's break down what it actually is, what it does, and how to use it right.

On the label it's called snail secretion filtrate — the mucus snails produce, rich in glycoproteins and hydrating compounds. Producers say it's collected without harming the snails — though practices vary.
It's rich in hyaluronic acid and glycoproteins — a genuine hydration boost. Studies also link it to barrier repair and calmer skin, and over time, fading post-acne marks.
Here's the part people skip: apply it to damp skin, pat it in — don't rub — then seal it with your moisturizer.
So — worth the goo? The evidence says it's a solid hydrator. Give it a try, and subscribe for more skincare, minus the hype.
